g.text: Tuesday 21 July, 10:00. Every morning since April the nightly service has loaded the same nine
statements into the context before the first question, whether the question concerned them or not.
"It reads all nine to tell me the time," Okafor says.
"It does not read all nine," you say. "They do not fit. It reads what is left of them."
You replace the statements with a list: account, bank, a line on what each holds. And two tools, one to
Varma is cautious. "Then it reads only what it chooses to."
"And if it chooses not to open the one that matters?"
The nine statements, as loaded every morning
the whole input: 37,669 tokens against a limit of 7,592 (30,077 over). Nothing was sent.
times the window. In trail order
fit. For three months the server has
cut this to about half a window each morning and answered from what was left.
. The trail, from the statements themselves
Every hop from Corvane Trading Ltd, computed from the statements
hops. No model wrote this table:
follows the debits. It is what each trace below
. Up front: a digest of every statement
Reach Holdings Ltd -> Pellmar Nominees Ltd.
. Just in time: a list and two tools
The same task, five ways of giving LANTERN the statements
a described list: the whole report
FLOW: Corvane Trading Ltd -> Lowmarsh Shipping Services Ltd | 9 payments | total 2262000.00 FLOW: Corvane
Trading Ltd -> Sabran Commercial Bank | 3 payments | total 180.00 FLOW: Corvane Trading Ltd -> Northwind
With the list, LANTERN opened corvane-trading.csv and stopped. Nothing failed and nothing was cut. It chose
not to open the next one.
. What it opened is part of the record
A sentence in the rules telling LANTERN not to finish early:
. The same condition checked in code,
A described list, and a check: request by request
. Never opened: Northwind Freight Ltd, Arden Logistics Ltd. A finding now comes with the list
of statements read to reach it, and the list of those that were not.
The nine statements the nightly service loads come to 37,669 tokens against a window of 8,192; 1 fit,
and the request is now refused where it used to be cut. With a digest of every statement loaded up front
LANTERN reported 6 of 7 hops in one request of 1,179 tokens. With a list of the files and two tools it
opened 1 statement and reported 1; with file names that say nothing, 1; told in a sentence not to finish
early, 1. With the same condition checked in code and the report sent back 6 times, it opened 7
statements and reported 7 of 7, totals right on 7, in 14 requests and 23,899 tokens. Each trace records
which statements were opened and which never were.
